newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories edge up in September.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories edge up in September.

text.p: Overall stocks of goods on the shelves of businesses edged up slightly in September, the government said on Friday, posting the smallest increase since June, when inventories barely budged.
Total business inventories rose just 0.1 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted $1 trillion after advancing by a revised 0.3 percent in August, the Commerce Department said.
The department had previously reported that August inventories had risen 0.5 percent.
Wall Street economists had expected September inventories to rise by 0.2 percent.
Retail inventories rose 0.8 percent to $313.55 billion, following an increase of 0.7 percent in August.
Automobile inventories, which are reflected in the retail figures, rose 1.4 percent to $89.49 billion in September.
Manufacturers' inventories increased by 0.3 percent to $437.13 billion in September after an increase of 0.3 percent in August.

Wholesalers' inventories were down 1.3 percent to $255.52 billion after falling a revised 0.1 percent in August. The department previously said wholesalers' inventories had advanced 0.5 percent in August.
Total business sales in September jumped 0.8 percent to $723.45 billion, after a revised 0.2 percent drop in August that was previously reported as a 0.3 percent decline.
The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace -- fell to 1.39 month's worth in September from 1.40 in August.
The ratio in September stood at its lowest level since the department began tracking that data, matching levels posted in July and May 1996.
